_comment: The chapter 6 section 6.4 `service_version` manifest for the service that implements
`lung_nodule`. The `spec` block below validates against the platform's own schema --
`medos.registry.schemas.schema_for_kind('service_version')` -- and
tests/integration/test_lung_nodule.py asserts that rather than asserting it here.
IT IS NOT PUBLISHED AS AN `artifacts` ROW, AND THE REASON IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT.
`MOS-REG-025` requires `spec.models[]` to be non-empty in `mode: native` and every
`ref` to resolve to a `model_version` artifact whose `lifecycle_status` is VALIDATED
or APPROVED at publish time. The `model_version` schema in turn makes
`evaluation_run_id` REQUIRED, matching `^er_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{10,26}$`.
This capability has no EvaluationRun. Its AcceptanceCriteria status is `unmet`, its
`evidence_reference` is null, and no cohort has been measured. Publishing it would
mean minting an `er_...` id for a run that never happened -- fabricated evidence, in
the one field the deployment gate reads. So the row is NOT written, and the blocker is
REPORTED instead.
The blocker is a real one and it is general, not a property of this capability:
chapter 6's own lifecycle (`MOS-REG-020`) has DRAFT and REGISTERED states that
PRECEDE VALIDATED, but a manifest that cannot omit `evaluation_run_id` cannot be
registered before it has been evaluated. `MOS-REG-047` sharpens it: it REQUIRES a
deterministic capability ('`emphysema_laa` MUST be served in 0.1.0 by a deterministic
measurement rather than a learned model') while `MOS-REG-025` requires every native
ServiceVersion to reference a ModelVersion. A threshold has no weights, so the
ModelVersion it must reference describes a parameter set -- which `weights_availability`
has no value for (`platform_managed` and `vendor_sealed` are the only two).
`models[0].ref` below therefore names an artifact that is DECLARED and not published.
A `publish()` of this manifest fails on the dangling ref, which is `MOS-REG-025`
working correctly.
_engineering_acceptance_note: `p95_wall_clock_seconds: 45` is a DECLARED engineering bar, NOT a measured p95. Three
studies are not a distribution and this manifest does not pretend otherwise; the bar
is set well above what was observed so that it is a ceiling rather than a claim.
What WAS measured, on one machine, is the detection stage alone, across repeated runs:
4.1-4.7 s on LIDC-IDRI-0001 (133 slices, 2.5 mm), 8.1 s on LIDC-IDRI-0002 (261 slices,
1.25 mm) and 9.3-10.1 s on LIDC-IDRI-0019 (305 slices, 1.25 mm). The spread between
repeats of the same study is filesystem cache, not algorithmic variance -- the detector
is deterministic, which tests/integration/test_lung_nodule.py asserts directly.
Building the canonical volume is the platform's work, not the service's, and is not
`MOS-REG-049`: this block carries ENGINEERING bars only. Every clinical threshold
lives in the Capability's AcceptanceCriteria and NONE of those numbers appears here;
the registry MUST reject a service_version that declares clinical acceptance
thresholds in its own manifest, and test_lung_nodule.py asserts the separation.
_operating_points_note: `operating_points` is ABSENT, and it took a spec contradiction to get there.
`MOS-SVC-020`: 'capabilities[].operating_points ... MUST be empty when and only when
`deterministic: true`'. This capability has no score anywhere, so by that rule the
member must be present and empty.
The platform's own schema refuses exactly that. `operating_points` carries
`minItems: 1`, so `"operating_points": []` -- the form MOS-SVC-020 mandates -- fails
validation. The member is OPTIONAL (`required` is `[id, outputs]`), so omission is the
only representable way to say 'no operating points'.
And the condition MOS-SVC-020 attaches the rule to cannot be written down either:
there is no `deterministic` member anywhere in the service_version manifest schema.
REPORTED, not patched. The schema is not edited to admit the empty array, because
`medos/medos/registry/schemas.py` is core and `MOS-REL-020` is the question of whether this
capability needs a core edit. It does not -- omission works -- but the contradiction
is real and belongs in the register, not in a commit message.
`MOS-SVC-021` still applies with full force: no sensitivity, specificity or PPV may be
displayed for this capability on any surface, because there is no threshold to report
